claim: A gain byte over this type's low shelf does not build the shelf at the gain it names either, and it does not reach it the way the two mid sections of the same type are reached. One shelf is stored at the bottom of the printed range -- the full cut -- and the byte blends the dry path towards that, with a boost being the same section with its numerator and its denominator exchanged. In coefficients it is the same three multiply-accumulates the mid sections use, moved from the numerator to the denominator, and the two are not the same curve: the mid reading has the low shelf falling away half an octave sooner in the middle of the window than the unit does, and this one is out by a quarter of a band.
whyNotNamed: Which end of the range a part stores a section at is not visible from outside it any more than whether it blends at run time or holds a row per setting. What is claimed is the curve, and the two things about the part that produce it -- one stored section rather than one per gain, and a far side that costs no second section -- together with which end the stored one sits at, which is what this record separates and what the mid sections answer the other way.
adds: The record says what each setting of the low shelf's gain did to the band profile. This claim is the step from that to how the byte reaches the shelf, which no record says. What it adds over the claim beside it is that the answer the mid sections gave does not carry: the same four readings, the same type, the same run, and the shelves come back on the other side. Every model in this archive builds its shelves at the gain, which is the third of the four.
refutedBy: A shelf at half its gain falling away where the width of the stored full-scale boost would put it, or where the section built at that gain would. Or a boost whose shape is not its cut's, at more than the one band this reading resolves. Or the same reading on another type's shelf coming back the mid sections' way.
whatItWouldChange: A renderer of this line building its shelves at the gain asked for is right at the ends of the byte and puts the shelf's own transition half an octave out in between, which is most of what a shelf at a modest setting sounds like. A renderer that took the mid sections' answer and carried it across to the shelves -- the obvious thing to do with the claim beside this one -- would be wrong by twice that, and in the other direction.

eraPriors.claim: Blending one stored section against the dry path costs the same whichever end of the range the stored one sits at.
eraPriors.why: Mixing a section's transfer towards unity in the numerator leaves its denominator alone; mixing it in the denominator leaves its numerator alone. Three multiply-accumulates between two stored rows either way, and a part has no reason of cost to prefer one. So which end it stores is decided by something else, and is worth reading off a unit rather than assumed.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: One of the two spellings needed a coefficient the other did not, which would make this a cost argument and not a measurement.

eraPriors.claim: A first order shelf's cut is its boost turned over.
eraPriors.why: A one-pole one-zero shelf at a gain and at its negative are the same pole and zero exchanged, so a part that has either has the other for one coefficient swap -- the same swap the peaking section uses, and the reason neither kind of section needs a second stored row for the far side of its byte.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: A cut of the same height as a boost came back a different shape, which is what the fourth reading in this class predicts and what the cut side of this record was read for.

alternatives.reading: The shelf is stored at the top of the printed range and the dry path is blended towards it, which is what the two mid sections of this same type do.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: It is wrong at every setting the reading places -- 16 of 16 -- and it is wrong the other way from all the others: it has the shelf falling away 0.601 octaves sooner than the unit on average, which is seven bands against the one this reading resolves. It is also the worst residual of the four. That the winner on the mid sections is the last of four here is the finding and not an inconsistency: the two are mirror images of each other and this record tells them apart.

alternatives.reading: The shelf is the one-pole section computed at the gain the byte names, or read out of a row stored per setting, which is the same curve.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: It says the shelf falls away at nearly the same distance at every setting, because a one-pole shelf's pole and zero part by the gain and the shape between them barely changes. The unit's figure moves half an octave across the window and this reading's moves a tenth: 13 of 16 settings wrong, out by 0.332 octaves on average.

alternatives.reading: The same blend with a second section stored at the other end of the range for the other side of the byte, rather than one section turned over.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: It is the winner on the cut side and cannot be told from it there, because a blend towards a stored cut is exactly what this claim says the cut is. On the boost side it is the reading that was ruled out above: 7 of 16 settings wrong, all of them boosts. A shelf whose boost is its cut turned over is what the unit has, and it is what a coefficient swap gives for nothing.

alternatives.reading: The high shelf is reached the same way as the low one, so this is a fact about shelves rather than about this shelf.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: A high shelf was asked and it is reached the same way. Not the slot this alternative named -- it named the standalone type's, and what was run is a combination type's pair, which is the mechanism the reading proposed rather than the address it pointed at. On that type both shelves store the cut: the high shelf's transition moves outwards as the shelf shrinks, which is the reading this claim closed on, and it is 0 of 4 settings out of place against 4 for the opposite end and 4 for the section built at its gain. The reading that wanted one row shared between a type's two shelves needed the high one to move inwards. It does not. data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-bands/04-01-10-the-shelves-a-combination-type-does-not-print-a-corner-for-in-twelfths.json.

residual.why: Reported and not read. All four candidates carry the same shelf, so the separation between them was never the renderer's; every one of their residuals falls and the ordering, the properties contradicted and the verdict are unchanged.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// roland-sc8850-01  ·  01 00  ·  section-gain
//
// Generated by yarn sync from inferences/models/shelf-mixed-with-the-dry-path-in-the-denominator.json.
// The claim it closes: inferences/roland-sc8850-01/section-gain-a-shelf-stores-the-cut.json
//
// Every constant, every section count and every structural choice below is
// the model's. The difference equations are the ordinary realisations of the
// sections the model names — this site's arithmetic, not a measurement.
//
// Compared against the unit over:
//   40 03 04: Settings [53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 59, 60, 62, 63, 66, 68, 69, 70, 72, 73, 74] on one record, which are one to eleven steps from the centre of the window on both sides, of which the reading places sixteen
//   40 03 06: Three settings on one record and nine on another, all of them the window's ends or past them or its centre, so this address separates nothing here
//   stimulus: A held note through the effect, its takes read as the energy of each twelfth octave against the run's own flat repeats.
//
// Outside that domain this says nothing: The high shelf of this type, which is scored and
// cannot answer. Every other type that prints a gain against a shelf. The two mid sections
// of this type, which are a claim of their own and answer the other way. Settings the
// reading does not place, which are named. What the part stores rather than computes,
// which no reading of an output reaches.
//
// Residual: 0.0022 median, 0.003 worst, in the median residual in decibels over the span the byte commands, meaned over the records that carry a feature.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#include <cmath>

namespace soundings::roland_sc8850_01::type_01_00 {

// The unit's own output ends between sixteen and eighteen kilohertz, measured: thirty-two
// decibels over silence at sixteen, sixteen at seventeen, nothing at eighteen. A chain
// running at thirty-two kilohertz ends exactly there. The rate is part of the candidate
// rather than a constant, so a reading above the half-rate is dropped by name instead of
// being answered with a number the model never said.
constexpr double kSampleRateHz = 32000.0;
constexpr double kPi = 3.14159265358979323846;

/**
 * A first-order shelf: one pole, one zero, tilting the two sides of its corner
 * against each other. `(s + w0 * V) / (s + w0)` for a low shelf and
 * `(V * s + w0) / (s + w0)` for a high one, bilinear-transformed.
 */
struct Shelf1 {
  enum class Side { Low, High };

  double b0 = 1.0, b1 = 0.0, a1 = 0.0, x1 = 0.0, y1 = 0.0;

  void set(double hz, double gainDb, Side side) {
    const double v = std::pow(10.0, gainDb / 20.0);
    const double k = std::tan(kPi * hz / kSampleRateHz);
    const double norm = 1.0 / (1.0 + k);
    a1 = (k - 1.0) * norm;
    if (side == Side::Low) {
      b0 = (1.0 + v * k) * norm;
      b1 = (v * k - 1.0) * norm;
    } else {
      b0 = (v + k) * norm;
      b1 = (k - v) * norm;
    }
  }

  double process(double x) {
    const double y = b0 * x + b1 * x1 - a1 * y1;
    x1 = x;
    y1 = y;
    return y;
  }
};

/** A second-order section, set the way the audio cookbook sets one. */
struct Biquad {
  enum class Side { Low, High };

  double b0 = 1.0, b1 = 0.0, b2 = 0.0, a1 = 0.0, a2 = 0.0;
  double x1 = 0.0, x2 = 0.0, y1 = 0.0, y2 = 0.0;

  void setShelf(double hz, double gainDb, Side side) {
    const double a = std::pow(10.0, gainDb / 40.0);
    const double w = 2.0 * kPi * hz / kSampleRateHz;
    const double cs = std::cos(w);
    // Unit slope, which is what `order 2` means here.
    const double alpha = std::sin(w) / 2.0 * std::sqrt(2.0);
    const double two = 2.0 * std::sqrt(a) * alpha;
    const double sign = side == Side::Low ? 1.0 : -1.0;
    const double a0 = (a + 1.0) - sign * (a - 1.0) * cs + two;
    b0 = a * ((a + 1.0) + sign * (a - 1.0) * cs + two) / a0;
    b1 = sign * 2.0 * a * ((a - 1.0) + sign * (a + 1.0) * cs) / a0;
    b2 = a * ((a + 1.0) + sign * (a - 1.0) * cs - two) / a0;
    a1 = -sign * 2.0 * ((a - 1.0) - sign * (a + 1.0) * cs) / a0;
    a2 = ((a + 1.0) - sign * (a - 1.0) * cs - two) / a0;
  }

  void setPeaking(double hz, double gainDb, double q) {
    const double a = std::pow(10.0, gainDb / 40.0);
    const double w = 2.0 * kPi * hz / kSampleRateHz;
    const double alpha = std::sin(w) / (2.0 * q);
    const double a0 = 1.0 + alpha / a;
    b0 = (1.0 + alpha * a) / a0;
    b1 = -2.0 * std::cos(w) / a0;
    b2 = (1.0 - alpha * a) / a0;
    a1 = b1;
    a2 = (1.0 - alpha / a) / a0;
  }

  double process(double x) {
    const double y = b0 * x + b1 * x1 + b2 * x2 - a1 * y1 - a2 * y2;
    x2 = x1;
    x1 = x;
    y2 = y1;
    y1 = y;
    return y;
  }
};

/** The chain the model names, in the order it names it. */
struct Effect {
  Shelf1 shelf0;
  Biquad peaking1;
  Biquad peaking2;
  Shelf1 shelf3;
  double gain4 = 1.0;

  void prepare(int b40_03_03, int b40_03_04, int b40_03_07, int b40_03_09, int b40_03_08, int b40_03_0A, int b40_03_0C, int b40_03_0B, int b40_03_05, int b40_03_06, int b40_03_16) {
    shelf0.set(shelf0CornerHz(b40_03_03), shelf0GainDb(b40_03_04), Shelf1::Side::Low);
    peaking1.setPeaking(peaking1CentreHz(b40_03_07), peaking1GainDb(b40_03_09), peaking1Q(b40_03_08));
    peaking2.setPeaking(peaking2CentreHz(b40_03_0A), peaking2GainDb(b40_03_0C), peaking2Q(b40_03_0B));
    shelf3.set(shelf3CornerHz(b40_03_05), shelf3GainDb(b40_03_06), Shelf1::Side::High);
    gain4 = std::pow(10.0, (gain4GainDb(b40_03_16)) / 20.0);
  }

  double process(double x) {
    x = shelf0.process(x);
    x = peaking1.process(x);
    x = peaking2.process(x);
    x = shelf3.process(x);
    x *= gain4;
    return x;
  }
};

extra.key: a note on the two halves of this class
extra.text: The mid sections and the shelves of one type were put to the same four readings on records from the same runs, and they answered oppositely: the peaks store the boost and the shelves store the cut. The first scoring of the shelves was done with the peaks' instrument -- the count of bands a feature stands over half its height in -- which on a shelf counts up from the bottom of the band set, and under it the shelves merely refused the blend without saying what stood instead. The reading that answered is a shelf's own, and the candidate it found was not in the class at the time: three readings were scored, all three were wrong, and the one that fits was written because the runner-up fitted one half of the byte and its mirror fitted the other.
